items.title: 4.8 Theoretical yield, actual yield and percentage yield

source_refs.note: Topic 4.8, printed pages 89-91; Sample Problem 4.20 (with its printed slips noted) and Quick Check 4.10 as the self-check.

blocks.title: Actual and theoretical yield
blocks.text: The amount of product obtained in a chemical reaction is the actual yield. The amount calculated from the balanced equation is the theoretical yield: the maximum amount of product that a given amount of reactant can produce according to the balanced equation.

In most reactions the product obtained is less than the theoretical yield, for these reasons: processes such as filtration, separation by distillation or a separating funnel, washing, drying and crystallization, if not properly carried out, decrease the actual yield; some reactants may take part in a competing side reaction and reduce the amount of the desired product; and a reaction may be reversible, so the backward reaction reduces the product. A chemist is interested in the efficiency of a reaction, expressed by comparing the actual and theoretical yields as a percentage: percentage yield = actual yield / theoretical yield x 100. The greater the percentage yield, the higher the efficiency.

Aspirin, C9H8O4 (180.16 g/mol), is prepared by heating salicylic acid, C7H6O3 (138.12 g/mol), with acetic anhydride, C4H6O3 (163.93 g/mol): C7H6O3 + C4H6O3 gives C9H8O4 + CH3COOH, one mole to one mole. With 3.00 g of salicylic acid and 6.00 g of acetic anhydride: salicylic acid = 3.00 / 138.12 = 0.022 mol; acetic anhydride = 6.00 / 163.93 = 0.037 mol. Salicylic acid is the limiting reactant and controls the yield of aspirin. 0.022 mol of salicylic acid gives 0.022 mol of aspirin, a theoretical yield of 0.022 x 180.16 = 3.96 g. With an actual yield of 2.85 g, percentage yield = 2.85 / 3.96 x 100 = 71.97 per cent.
